\section{Supplementary Methods}

\bmhead{S1. Label processing}
ABoVE version 2\cite{Moore2025} contains \nqcAboveRaw{} thaw-depth records; after restricting to probe measurements in August--October with $0<\mathrm{ALT}<300$ cm within 45--80$^\circ$N, \nqcAboveKept{} records remained, and \nqcAboveEarly{} measurements from January--July were excluded as early-season values. CALM\cite{Streletskiy2025} contributed \nqcCalmSy{} site-years in Alaska and Canada, of which \nqcCalmNoloc{} could not be assigned to a 1 km cell, giving \nqcCalmCy{} cell-years. ALLena\cite{Veremeeva2025} contains \nqcLenaRaw{} records, of which \nqcLenaEos{} are August--September values without the measurement-limit flag; the seasonal maximum per location and year gave \nqcLenaCy{} cell-years. Of the \nqcTotalCy{} cell-years of all years, \nqcTotalCyIn{} fall in 2010--2024 and have year-specific climate input. Multiple measurements in a cell and year were averaged, and the mean day of year was kept for the accumulation of TDD.

\bmhead{S2. Climate variables}
All variables are computed from monthly ERA5-Land means for each cell and year $y$ (days per month $d_m$). TDD $=\sum_{m\in y}\max(T_m,0)\,d_m$; the cumulative TDD to the end of each month gives the observation-day value by linear interpolation in the day of year. Freezing degree-days use October $y-1$ to April $y$; the snow water equivalent is the mean of October $y-1$ to September $y$; the soil temperature is the mean of the top ERA5-Land soil layer (0--7 cm). Cells over sea in ERA5-Land use the nearest land cell within $\pm$0.2$^\circ$ and then $\pm$0.5$^\circ$. The mean climate input is the 2011--2024 mean of the yearly values (2010 is excluded because its winter variables are incomplete).

\bmhead{S3. Product extraction and training data}
Yearly products were sampled at the cell centre for the observation year: Wei et al.\cite{Wei2026} from the 1 km EPSG:3995 rasters, Liu et al.\cite{Liu2024} from the 1/120$^\circ$ rasters, ESA CCI v4 and v5\cite{Westermann2024,Westermann2025} from the yearly NetCDF files, and Yi and Kimball\cite{YiKimball2019} from the Alaska NetCDF. Aalto et al.\cite{Aalto2018} provide one baseline value (2000--2014). Wei et al. were trained on 201 CALM and GTN-P sites with 2,196 annual observations of 2000--2020 and publish the site coordinates; the median distance from our label cells to the nearest site is \ndistweiAkmed{} km in Alaska, \ndistweiLemed{} km in the Lena Delta and \ndistweiCamed{} km in Canada (Supplementary Fig.~S5). Liu et al. were trained on 2,966 site-years from CALM, an earlier version of the ABoVE data (2008--2020), ABCflux and Tibetan sites. ESA CCI is a process model with remotely sensed land-surface temperature and is not trained on ALT observations. Mean product biases by latitude band (prediction minus observation) were computed on the label cell-years with a product value of the observation year.

\bmhead{S4. External CALM regions}
The CALM data set\cite{Streletskiy2025} contains \nextRawSy{} site-years of 2010--2024 outside Alaska, Canada and mountain permafrost. \nextCens{} censored value (for example `$>$260') and \nextQcRm{} values with comments indicating early measurement, burning, flooding or a probe not reaching the permafrost table were removed, and sites within 100 km of the study labels were excluded. The remaining \nextcy{} cell-years in \nextcells{} cells were assigned to eight regions. Year-specific climate inputs, terrain and soil covariates and product values were computed with the same procedures as for the study regions.

\bmhead{S5. Product-anchored residual learning and SHAP}
In the product-anchored test, the product value $p$ of the observation year was recalibrated on the training fold as $a+bp$ (least squares), and the residual learner of the main model was trained on $y-(a+bp)$ with the same 23 features and $\lambda=0.5$. The test used the spatial-block folds of the main experiment and only the cell-years with a product value. SHAP values\cite{Lundberg2017} were computed with CatBoost's exact tree algorithm for the residual model ($y-\hat{y}_P$) and the direct model, both fitted to all labels of a region, and summarised as the mean absolute value per feature and per feature group.
